use_cases.name: Provision a new client tenant
use_cases.goal: Stand up an isolated, fully seeded and health-checked tenant for a signed client or approved demo request in under 30 minutes without manual database work.

stakeholders.interest: Receives a working tenant with a first administrator account and safe default roles on day one.
Can prove when, by whom and with what baseline configuration the tenant was created.
Starts configuration immediately instead of waiting on infrastructure tickets.

use_cases.trigger: A signed client order or an approved demo request is assigned to the implementation consultant.
preconditions: The implementation consultant is authenticated and holds the tenant-provisioning permission.
The client's legal name, intended tenant code, edition and data-residency choice (cloud region in India by default) are recorded on the order.
postconditions_success: A tenant exists with its own isolation key, and every table query is filtered by that key.
Baseline reference data, default role templates and a tenant default approval chain are seeded.
A first tenant admin principal exists in Pending activation state and an activation link has been issued.
The provisioning run is recorded in the audit ledger with duration and health-check results.
postconditions_failure: No partially created tenant remains; every artefact of the failed run is rolled back.
The provisioning request shows status Failed with the failing check named, and the consultant is notified.

main_flow.action: Opens a provisioning request with client legal name, tenant code, edition, data-residency region and planned go-live date.
Validates that the tenant code is unique and well-formed, then allocates an isolated tenant partition keyed on tenant_id.
Seeds baseline data: statutory picklists, role templates, notification templates and a tenant default approval chain.
Records the client's legal entities and locations with state codes, for example LE-01 with LOC-BLR and LOC-PLA.
Creates the first tenant admin principal with the tenant-admin role template and issues a time-limited activation link.
Runs the post-provisioning health check: cross-tenant isolation probe, default chain resolvable, audit write and event relay round trip.
Marks the tenant Ready, records elapsed time and check results in the audit ledger and notifies the consultant.
Activates the account through the link, enrols multi-factor authentication and confirms first sign-in.

alternate_flows.condition: The request is a demo request rather than a signed order.
steps: Nucleus platform seeds the synthetic Vindhya Precision Industries Pvt Ltd dataset in place of an empty tenant.
Nucleus platform sets an expiry date on the demo tenant and labels every screen as demonstration data.

alternate_flows.condition: The consultant chooses to start from a previously approved configuration package.
steps: Implementation consultant selects the package and reviews the list of objects it will create.
Nucleus platform applies the package as effective-dated configuration versions.

exception_flows.condition: The requested tenant code already exists or contains disallowed characters.
exception_flows.handling: Nucleus platform rejects the request with the reason and suggests an available code; nothing is allocated.

exception_flows.condition: Any health check fails, including a query that returns rows from another tenant.
exception_flows.handling: Nucleus platform rolls back the whole run, sets status Failed with the failing check named and raises an operations alert.

exception_flows.condition: Elapsed provisioning time exceeds 30 minutes.
exception_flows.handling: The tenant is still completed if checks pass, but the run is flagged as an NFR breach and counted on the operations dashboard.

nfrs: A tenant is fully provisioned, seeded and health-checked in under 30 minutes, end to end, with no manual step.
The isolation probe in the health check runs against every tenant-scoped table and must return zero foreign rows.

user_stories.want: to provision a client tenant from a single request form with automated seeding and checks
user_stories.so_that: configuration work can begin the same day the order is signed

acceptance.given: a signed order for Vindhya Precision Industries Pvt Ltd with tenant code vindhya and region set to a cloud region in India
acceptance.when: the consultant submits the provisioning request
acceptance.then: the tenant reaches status Ready in under 30 minutes and the audit ledger shows the run with its elapsed time

acceptance.given: a tenant named vindhya already exists
acceptance.when: the consultant submits another request with tenant code vindhya
acceptance.then: the request is rejected with the message that the code is in use and no partition is allocated

user_stories.want: to receive an activation link for the first administrator account of my new tenant
user_stories.so_that: I can take ownership of users and scope without asking the vendor for access

acceptance.given: the tenant vindhya has just reached status Ready
acceptance.when: the tenant admin opens the activation link within 72 hours
acceptance.then: the account is activated, multi-factor enrolment is required before the first screen loads, and the event platform.principal.created is recorded

acceptance.given: the activation link is older than 72 hours
acceptance.then: activation is refused and the consultant can reissue a new link from the provisioning request

user_stories.want: evidence that a newly provisioned tenant cannot read another tenant's rows
user_stories.so_that: tenant isolation is proven at creation rather than assumed

acceptance.given: tenants vindhya and a second demo tenant both hold employee records
acceptance.when: the provisioning health check runs its isolation probe as a vindhya principal
acceptance.then: zero rows from the second tenant are returned and the probe result is stored with the run

acceptance.given: the isolation probe returns any foreign row
acceptance.then: the run is marked Failed, the tenant is rolled back and an operations alert is raised

use_cases.name: Grant identity, role and data scope
use_cases.goal: Create a user or agent principal and grant it the narrowest entity, location and payroll-group scope its job needs, enforced on every request.

stakeholders.interest: Salary and rate structure of head-office-payrolled staff stay invisible to plant users.
Sees and edits attendance for every worker at the site, including head-office-payrolled staff.
Every grant names who granted it and from when it applies.
Personal data access follows least privilege as expected under the DPDP Act 2023 (to be validated by Legal).

use_cases.trigger: A user is created or moves role, entity or location, or a new agent is registered.
preconditions: The tenant admin is authenticated with a recent step-up and holds the principal-administration permission.
The legal entities, locations and payroll groups to be granted exist in the tenant.
postconditions_success: The principal exists with a role template, entity grants and location grants, each with granted_by and effective_from.
Every subsequent request by the principal is filtered by the intersection of tenant, entity, location, reporting line and payroll group.
Compensation fields of records outside the principal's payroll group are returned as null on every surface.
postconditions_failure: No principal or grant is persisted when a validation fails.
A principal whose scope cannot be resolved receives an empty result set, never a full one.

main_flow.action: Creates the principal (user, agent or service) on the scope grant screen and attaches a role template.
Grants entity scope by selecting one or more legal entity codes with an effective-from date.
Grants location scope by selecting one or more location codes and setting can_edit_time to Y or N.
On every request, resolves effective scope as tenant ∩ entity ∩ location ∩ reporting subtree ∩ payroll group.
Checks whether each requested field is a compensation field and whether the reader is outside the record's payroll group.

alternate_flows.condition: The field is not a compensation field, or the reader belongs to the record's payroll group.
steps: Nucleus platform returns the field value unchanged within the resolved scope.

alternate_flows.condition: The principal needs entity-wide time visibility and has no location grant.
steps: Tenant admin sets the explicit entity-wide time visibility flag with a reason.
Nucleus platform records the flag as a grant with granted_by and effective_from.

exception_flows.condition: An agent principal is submitted without a named human owner.
exception_flows.handling: Creation fails with the reason that an accountable owner is mandatory; nothing is persisted.

exception_flows.condition: A principal has no location grant and no entity-wide time flag.
exception_flows.handling: The principal sees no time data for any location until a location grant is added.

exception_flows.condition: Scope resolution fails because a grant, reporting line or payroll group cannot be read.
exception_flows.handling: Nucleus platform returns an empty set and logs the failure; it never falls back to a wider scope.

exception_flows.condition: The reader is outside the record's payroll group and the field is basic, da, hra, daily_rate, gross or ctc.
exception_flows.handling: The field is returned as null on screens, reports, exports and the API while attendance fields stay populated; the check runs in every build.

nfrs: Scope resolution adds no more than 20 ms at p95 to any read request.
The compensation-nulling golden test runs on every build and blocks release on failure.

user_stories.want: to register an agent principal only together with a named accountable human owner
user_stories.so_that: every automated action can be traced to a person who answers for it

acceptance.given: the tenant admin is creating a principal of type agent
acceptance.when: they save it with owner_principal_id empty
acceptance.then: the save fails with the message that an accountable human owner is required and no principal is created

acceptance.given: the same agent with owner_principal_id set to HR operations user E1006
acceptance.then: the principal is created and platform.principal.created is emitted with the owner recorded

user_stories.want: to grant a plant HR user location scope for one site with time-edit rights
user_stories.so_that: the user can run the site's time office without seeing other sites

acceptance.given: a plant HR user with entity grant LE-02 and location grant LOC-CHN with can_edit_time Y
acceptance.when: the user opens attendance for LOC-HYD
acceptance.then: no LOC-HYD records are returned

acceptance.given: the same user
acceptance.when: the user opens attendance for LOC-CHN
acceptance.then: attendance for every LOC-CHN worker is listed and editable, including head-office-payrolled staff

user_stories.want: to see attendance but never salary or rate data for head-office-payrolled employees at my site
user_stories.so_that: I can run the time office without exposure to compensation outside my payroll group

acceptance.given: a plant HR user scoped to LOC-CHN and payroll group PLANT-CHN, and employee E1056 Anand Krishnan at LOC-CHN in payroll group HO
acceptance.when: the user opens E1056's record, the salary register, an export and the API
acceptance.then: attendance fields are populated and basic, da, hra, daily_rate, gross and ctc are null on all four surfaces

acceptance.given: a payroll manager scoped to payroll group HO
acceptance.then: all compensation fields are shown with their values

user_stories.want: assurance that a failure in scope resolution never widens access
user_stories.so_that: a defect cannot silently expose an entire tenant

acceptance.then: an empty list is returned and a scope-resolution failure is logged with the principal ID

acceptance.given: a query issued with a defect that omits the tenant filter
acceptance.then: row-level isolation still blocks every row from other tenants

use_cases.name: Author and effective-date configuration
use_cases.goal: Change a client policy as a versioned, effective-dated, simulated and approved configuration object rather than as code.

stakeholders.interest: Policy changes take effect on the agreed date and old periods keep the old rules.
A rerun of a past period uses the configuration that applied then.
Every configuration version shows who changed it, why and when it applies.

use_cases.trigger: A client policy changes or an implementation requires a new rule set.
preconditions: The implementation consultant holds the implementation role for the tenant.
The configuration object type (for example a leave policy) exists in the tenant.
postconditions_success: A new configuration version exists with valid_from, change reason and approver, and the prior version is end-dated, not deleted.
Computations dated before valid_from continue to read the prior version.
postconditions_failure: The draft remains unpublished and the active version is unchanged.

main_flow.action: Opens the configuration object, for example a leave policy on the leave policy configuration screen, and creates a draft version.
Edits the parameters and enters the effective-from date and a change reason.
Validates the draft against its schema and dependent objects, such as leave types referenced by accrual rules.
Runs a simulation on a sample population and reviews per-employee before-and-after results.
Submits the draft for approval with the simulation summary attached.
Approves the configuration change through the shared approval engine.
Publishes the draft as a new version from the effective date and end-dates the superseded version without deleting it.
Writes an audit entry and emits a versioning event for downstream caches and consumers.

alternate_flows.condition: The effective date falls in a past period.
steps: Nucleus platform lists the closed payroll and attendance periods the change would touch.
Implementation consultant confirms the retro change explicitly before the draft can be submitted.

alternate_flows.condition: The client rule cannot be expressed with the available configuration parameters.
steps: Implementation consultant records the rule as a product gap with the client's worked example.
The draft is saved but not submitted until the gap is resolved.

exception_flows.condition: Another published or pending version already starts on the same effective date.
exception_flows.handling: Validation fails and names the conflicting version; the consultant must change the date or withdraw the other draft.

exception_flows.condition: The simulation reports errors such as a negative leave balance for any employee.
exception_flows.handling: Submission is disabled until the errors are resolved or each is acknowledged with a reason.

exception_flows.condition: The approver rejects the change.
exception_flows.handling: The draft returns to the consultant with the reason; the active version is unchanged.

nfrs: A simulation over 5,000 employees completes in under 60 seconds.
Configuration version history is retained for the life of the tenant.

user_stories.want: to publish a leave policy change that applies only from a future date
user_stories.so_that: current-year balances are untouched while next year's rules are ready in advance

acceptance.given: the active casual leave policy grants 6 days a year
acceptance.when: the consultant publishes a version granting 8 days effective 2027-01-01
acceptance.then: a request dated 2026-12-15 reads the 6-day version and a request dated 2027-01-10 reads the 8-day version

acceptance.given: the 8-day version is published
acceptance.then: the 6-day version is still listed with recorded_to set and no row has been deleted

user_stories.want: to simulate a configuration change against real employees before submitting it
user_stories.so_that: I catch side effects before they reach payslips or balances

acceptance.given: a draft accrual rule and a sample of 70 employees from LE-01
acceptance.then: a per-employee before-and-after table is shown with differences highlighted

acceptance.given: the simulation shows employee E1028 with a negative balance
acceptance.then: the submit action is disabled until the error is fixed or acknowledged with a reason

user_stories.want: to read the configuration that applied on a given date
user_stories.so_that: I can verify a past computation against the rules in force at that time

acceptance.given: two versions of a policy effective 2026-04-01 and 2026-10-01
acceptance.when: the auditor requests the policy as at 2026-07-15
acceptance.then: the 2026-04-01 version is returned with its approver and change reason

acceptance.given: the same request with recorded_at set to 2026-05-01
acceptance.then: only versions recorded on or before 2026-05-01 are considered

use_cases.name: Define and version an approval workflow
use_cases.goal: Publish a new or changed approval chain definition as a version so that new requests use it while in-flight requests finish on the version they started under.

stakeholders.interest: Pending items in the inbox do not change approver or step count midway.
A request submitted yesterday is decided under the rules that applied when it was submitted.
Chains can change when the organisation changes, without a code release.

use_cases.trigger: A new approvable process is introduced or an existing chain must change.
preconditions: The request type exists and is wired to the shared approval engine.
A tenant default chain exists for fallback routing.
postconditions_success: A new chain version exists with effective_from, keys (request type, worker class, location, amount band), steps and SLA hours.
Instances started before publication continue on their original version; new submissions bind to the new version.
postconditions_failure: The previous chain version remains in force and the draft stays unpublished.

main_flow.action: Selects a request type, for example leave application, and creates a draft chain version.
Sets the resolution keys the chain applies to: worker class, location and amount band.
Adds ordered steps, each with approver resolution mode (role, position or named person) and SLA hours.
Sets the reroute policy for departed approvers and the escalation target for SLA breach on each step.
Validates that every step can resolve an approver and that the keys do not overlap another active chain.
Simulates sample requests and reviews the approver resolved at each step.
Publishes the version with an effective-from date and a change reason.
Binds new submissions to the new version and leaves in-flight instances pinned to their starting version.

alternate_flows.condition: The consultant schedules the version for a future date.
steps: Nucleus platform keeps the current version active until the effective date.
At the effective date, new submissions start binding to the new version.

exception_flows.condition: A step's role or position has no current holder in some location covered by the keys.
exception_flows.handling: Validation fails and lists the uncovered locations; publication is blocked.

exception_flows.condition: No reroute policy is set for a step resolved by named person.
exception_flows.handling: Validation fails because a departed approver would leave items orphaned.

exception_flows.condition: Two active chains match the same request type, worker class, location and amount band.
exception_flows.handling: Validation fails and names the overlapping chain, since each request must resolve to exactly one chain.

nfrs: Publishing a chain version never alters the step count or approvers of an in-flight instance.
Chain resolution for a submitted request completes in under 100 ms at p95.

user_stories.want: to publish a new chain version without disturbing requests already in progress
user_stories.so_that: approvers and requesters never see a request change its route midway

acceptance.given: a two-step leave chain v1 and a leave request from E1018 pending at step 1
acceptance.then: E1018's request still shows two steps and completes on v1

acceptance.given: v2 is published
acceptance.when: employee E1019 submits a new leave request
acceptance.then: the new instance binds to v2 and shows three steps

user_stories.want: to simulate which approver each step would resolve to for a sample request
user_stories.so_that: I can confirm routing before the chain goes live

acceptance.given: a draft chain for leave at LOC-PLA with step 1 resolved by reporting manager
acceptance.when: the consultant simulates a request from E1018
acceptance.then: step 1 resolves to E1017 Nikhil Iyer

acceptance.given: a draft step resolved by a position with no incumbent at LOC-PUN
acceptance.then: publication is blocked and LOC-PUN is listed as uncovered

user_stories.want: every chain version to record who published it, when and why
user_stories.so_that: routing changes can be reviewed after a dispute

acceptance.given: a chain version published on 2026-11-05 by the implementation consultant
acceptance.when: the tenant admin opens the chain history
acceptance.then: the version shows publisher, timestamp, effective_from and change reason

acceptance.given: the consultant tries to publish without a change reason
acceptance.then: publication is refused with a message asking for the reason

use_cases.name: Execute an approval chain
use_cases.goal: Route any approvable request through its configured chain to a recorded final decision, with SLA tracking, rerouting and auditable HR override.

stakeholders.interest: Gets a timely decision and the reason for any rejection.
Sees every pending item from every module in one inbox with the rule context.
Can correct or close a request at any stage with the change on record.
Each decision records actor, time, channel and reason.

use_cases.trigger: A requester submits any approvable request: leave, gate pass, loan, requisition, overtime, regularisation or letter.
preconditions: The requester is authenticated and the request has passed its own form validation.
A chain is configured for the request or a tenant default chain exists.
postconditions_success: The approval instance is closed with final state, closed_at and every step decision recorded.
The domain-specific approved event is emitted and control returns to the calling process.
postconditions_failure: On rejection the instance ends, the requester is notified with the reason, and the calling process receives the rejection.
No item is left without an active approver.

main_flow.action: Submits an approvable request; the engine reads the chain for tenant, request type, worker class and location and opens an instance.
Materialises the current step, resolves the approver by role, position or named person, and starts the SLA clock.
Approves, rejects or returns the item from the unified approval inbox; actor, timestamp, channel and reason are captured.
Checks whether any mandatory steps remain in the chain.
Closes the instance, emits the domain-specific approved event and hands control back to the calling process.
Overrides or edits the request at any stage when needed, recording actor and reason.

alternate_flows.condition: One or more mandatory steps remain.
steps: Nucleus platform opens the next step sequentially and resolves its approver.
The next approver receives the item in the unified approval inbox.

alternate_flows.condition: The approver returns the request for correction instead of deciding.
steps: Nucleus platform sends the request back to the requester with the return reason.
Employee / worker amends and resubmits; the instance resumes at the same step.

alternate_flows.condition: The approver decides from the business messaging channel or mobile app while offline.
steps: The decision is queued on the device and synchronised when connectivity returns.
Nucleus platform records the channel and the original decision time.

exception_flows.condition: No chain is configured for the request's type, worker class and location.
exception_flows.handling: The request routes to the tenant default chain and a configuration warning is raised to the implementation consultant.

exception_flows.condition: The resolved approver is inactive or has left.
exception_flows.handling: The step reroutes to the successor, then to the role holder; the item is never left orphaned.

exception_flows.condition: The resolved approver is the requester.
exception_flows.handling: Self-approval is not permitted; the step resolves to the next approver in the reporting line.

exception_flows.condition: The approver rejects or returns without entering a reason.
exception_flows.handling: The decision is refused until a reason is entered; on rejection the instance ends and the requester is notified with the reason text.

exception_flows.condition: A step's SLA expires before a decision.
exception_flows.handling: The item escalates per the step configuration and the breach is counted; the SLA is never silently extended.

exception_flows.condition: HR submits an override without a reason.
exception_flows.handling: The service rejects the override; the request state is unchanged.

nfrs: A decision recorded in the inbox is reflected in the calling module within 5 seconds at p95.
Decisions queued offline are synchronised within 60 seconds of reconnection without duplication.

user_stories.want: to decide every pending request from one inbox with the rule context shown
user_stories.so_that: I do not have to visit each module to clear approvals

acceptance.given: manager E1021 Rekha Deshpande has a leave request from E1022 and an overtime request from E1020 pending
acceptance.when: she opens the unified approval inbox
acceptance.then: both items are listed with request type, requester, SLA due time and the rule being applied

acceptance.given: she chooses Reject on the leave request with the reason field empty
acceptance.then: the decision is refused with a message that a reason is required

user_stories.want: to be told the reason when my request is rejected
user_stories.so_that: I can correct and resubmit without chasing my manager

acceptance.given: E1022's leave request is rejected at step 1 with reason 'Line audit on 12 Nov'
acceptance.then: the instance ends and E1022 receives a notification containing the reason text

acceptance.given: a request returned for correction
acceptance.when: the employee amends and resubmits it
acceptance.then: the instance resumes at the same step and the earlier return is visible in its history

user_stories.want: to edit or close a request at any stage with my reason on record
user_stories.so_that: operational corrections are possible without losing accountability

acceptance.given: leave request LV-2026-0774 is approved
acceptance.when: HR closes it on 14 Sep with reason 'Early return confirmed by supervisor'
acceptance.then: the audit entry records HR's identity, timestamp, previous state and reason, and platform.approval.overridden is emitted

acceptance.given: HR attempts an override with an empty reason
acceptance.then: the service rejects the override and the request state is unchanged

user_stories.want: items queued against a departed approver to reach me as the successor
user_stories.so_that: no request is stranded when someone leaves

acceptance.given: a loan request pending at a step resolved to an approver whose exit was processed on 30 Sep
acceptance.then: the step reroutes to the named successor and appears in the successor's inbox

acceptance.given: no successor is named
acceptance.then: the step resolves to the current role holder and the reroute is logged

use_cases.name: Write the audit and action ledger
use_cases.goal: Record every write and every sensitive read in one append-only ledger that names the real actor, including agent identity and its human owner.

stakeholders.interest: Can reconstruct who did what, on whose behalf and through which channel.
Access to PAN, Aadhaar, bank and salary data is evidenced for privacy obligations (to be validated by Legal).
Agent actions are traceable to their accountable owner.

use_cases.trigger: Any service commits a write or serves a read of a field classified as sensitive.
preconditions: The acting principal has been authenticated and its scope resolved.
Field security classifications are configured for sensitive fields.
postconditions_success: An immutable ledger entry exists with tenant, actor, on-behalf-of, agent owner where applicable, action, object, change digest, channel, IP and timestamp.
The entry is linked to the previous entry so tampering is detectable.
postconditions_failure: If the ledger entry cannot be written, the business write is rolled back; no unaudited write persists.

main_flow.action: Intercepts a committed write or a read that returns a field classified as sensitive.
Builds the entry: tenant, actor principal, real actor if delegated or act-as, agent owner, action and object reference.
Adds a before-and-after digest for writes, or the sensitive field classes revealed for reads, plus channel and source IP.
Appends the entry in the same transaction as the business write, chained to the previous entry's hash.
Queries the ledger read-only by object, actor, agent or date range within the auditor's scope.
Verifies hash-chain integrity nightly and reports the result to the auditor dashboard.

alternate_flows.condition: The actor is an agent principal.
steps: Nucleus platform records the agent principal as actor and its owner_principal_id as accountable owner on the same entry.
The entry is stored in the same ledger, with agent identity as a dimension.

exception_flows.condition: The ledger append fails.
exception_flows.handling: The business transaction is rolled back and the caller receives a retriable error.

exception_flows.condition: Any principal attempts to update or delete a ledger entry.
exception_flows.handling: The operation is refused and the attempt is itself recorded as a ledger entry.

exception_flows.condition: The nightly integrity check finds a broken hash link.
exception_flows.handling: A security incident is raised to the tenant admin and auditor with the first broken entry identified.

exception_flows.condition: An HR override arrives without a reason.
exception_flows.handling: The override is rejected before reaching the ledger, so no unexplained override is recorded as accepted.

nfrs: Ledger append adds no more than 10 ms at p95 to a write transaction.
Ledger entries are retained for at least 8 years and cannot be altered by any role, including tenant admin.

user_stories.want: to see agent actions in the same ledger as human actions with the owner named
user_stories.so_that: automated changes are reviewed with the same rigour as manual ones

acceptance.given: an agent principal owned by E1006 drafts a letter for E1043
acceptance.when: the auditor filters the ledger by object E1043
acceptance.then: the entry shows the agent as actor and E1006 as accountable owner

acceptance.given: the auditor filters by actor type agent for October 2026
acceptance.then: only agent-originated entries are returned, from the same ledger as human entries

user_stories.want: every view of an unmasked PAN or bank account to be logged
user_stories.so_that: access to sensitive identifiers can be evidenced on request

acceptance.given: a payroll manager unmasks E1056's PAN on the employee record
acceptance.then: a ledger entry records the reader, field class PAN, object E1056, channel and source IP

acceptance.given: the same payroll manager views the masked value only
acceptance.then: no sensitive-read entry is written for PAN

user_stories.want: the ledger to be impossible to edit even with my privileges
user_stories.so_that: the audit trail is credible to external auditors

acceptance.given: the tenant admin calls the delete operation on a ledger entry
acceptance.then: it is refused and a new entry records the attempted deletion

acceptance.given: the nightly integrity check
acceptance.then: the auditor dashboard shows the check as passed with the entry count verified

use_cases.name: Publish domain events through the outbox relay
use_cases.goal: Guarantee that every committed domain write publishes its event exactly once to consumers, and that no event is published for a write that rolled back.

stakeholders.interest: Payroll and journal events reach the ERP system once, never twice and never lost.
Event transport can change without modifying producing services.
Events can be replayed for dispute investigation.

use_cases.trigger: Any domain service commits a write that produces an event.
preconditions: The producing service writes its outbox row through the shared outbox library.
Each event type has a declared idempotency key.
postconditions_success: The outbox row is marked published with a timestamp, and every subscribed consumer has processed the event once.
postconditions_failure: Unpublished rows remain in the outbox and are retried; repeatedly failing rows are moved to a dead-letter store and an alert is raised.

main_flow.action: Writes the business change and an outbox row in the same database transaction.
Populates the outbox row with a CloudEvents envelope: id, type, source, tenant, subject, time and idempotency key.
Relay reads unpublished outbox rows per tenant in commit order.
Relay publishes each event to the configured transport and waits for acknowledgement.
Marks the outbox row published with the acknowledgement timestamp.
Receives the event, checks the idempotency key and processes it once.

alternate_flows.condition: The operations team switches the event transport.
steps: The relay is reconfigured to the new transport adapter.
Producers continue writing outbox rows unchanged; the relay resumes from the oldest unpublished row.

exception_flows.condition: The business transaction rolls back.
exception_flows.handling: The outbox row rolls back with it, so no event is ever published for an uncommitted change.

exception_flows.condition: The transport is unavailable.
exception_flows.handling: Rows stay unpublished and are retried with exponential backoff; none is dropped.

exception_flows.condition: An event fails 8 consecutive publish attempts.
exception_flows.handling: The row is moved to the dead-letter store, later events for other subjects continue, and an operations alert is raised.

exception_flows.condition: A consumer receives an event whose idempotency key it has already processed.

use_cases.name: Write bi-temporal versions and read as at a point in time
use_cases.goal: Keep every temporal fact as non-destructive versions on valid and recorded time so that any past state can be reproduced exactly.

stakeholders.interest: Rerunning a past period reproduces the same result from the same snapshot.
Attendance recompute uses the facts known at the recompute snapshot.
Can see both what was true and what was known at any moment.

use_cases.trigger: Any change to a temporal fact such as an assignment, salary structure or policy attribute, or any as-at read request.
preconditions: The table is declared temporal with valid_from, valid_to, recorded_from and recorded_to columns.
postconditions_success: A new version row exists; the superseded version carries recorded_to; no row has been deleted or updated in place.
As-at reads return the version valid at valid_at as known at recorded_at.
postconditions_failure: The write is rejected and the existing versions are unchanged.

main_flow.action: Opens a new version for the temporal fact with valid_from, valid_to, recorded_from, changed_by and change_reason.
End-dates the superseded version by setting recorded_to; the row is never deleted.
Serves as-at reads using caller-supplied valid_at and recorded_at, defaulting recorded_at to now.

alternate_flows.condition: The change corrects a past fact rather than recording a future change.
steps: Nucleus platform writes a version with the original valid_from and a new recorded_from.
Reads with recorded_at before the correction still return the uncorrected value.

exception_flows.condition: A service attempts to update a temporal row in place.
exception_flows.handling: The data layer rejects the update; only versioned writes are accepted.

exception_flows.condition: A payroll run or attendance recompute calls the as-at read without its snapshot timestamp.
exception_flows.handling: The read is rejected for derived work; the caller must pass the run or recompute snapshot timestamp.

exception_flows.condition: A delete is requested on a temporal row.
exception_flows.handling: The delete is refused; a closing version is written instead.

nfrs: An as-at read for a single record returns in under 50 ms at p95.
A payroll rerun with the same snapshot timestamp produces byte-identical results.

user_stories.want: a rerun of a closed period to read data as known at that run's snapshot
user_stories.so_that: later corrections do not silently change a result already paid

acceptance.then: the original basic is used and the result matches the paid run

use_cases.name: Enforce adaptive MFA and step-up authentication
use_cases.goal: Require multi-factor authentication for privileged roles and fresh re-authentication before high-risk actions.

stakeholders.interest: Privileged accounts cannot be used with a stolen password alone.
Bank details cannot be changed by someone holding a session left open.
Each high-risk action records the authentication strength used.

use_cases.trigger: A privileged user signs in, or any user starts a protected action: unmask an identifier, change bank details, approve payroll or grant a role.
preconditions: The tenant admin has configured the MFA policy, the list of privileged roles and the step-up window.
The user has at least one enrolled factor: TOTP, push approval or FIDO2 passkey.
postconditions_success: The protected action executes and the audit entry records the factor type and time of the last strong authentication.
postconditions_failure: The protected action is not executed; repeated failures lock the factor and alert the tenant admin.

main_flow.action: Configures the MFA policy: privileged roles, allowed factors (TOTP, push, FIDO2 passkey) and a step-up window of 5 minutes.
Signs in through the identity provider using OIDC or SAML 2.0, or with local credentials.
Detects a privileged role and evaluates risk signals such as a new device or unusual location.
Completes the requested second factor.
Starts a protected action, for example approving the October 2026 payroll for payroll group HO.
Checks the time since the last strong authentication and requests step-up when it exceeds the configured window.
Re-authenticates with an enrolled factor.
Executes the action and records factor type and authentication time in the audit ledger.

alternate_flows.condition: The last strong authentication is within the step-up window.
steps: Nucleus platform proceeds without a new challenge.

alternate_flows.condition: The identity provider asserts that MFA was already completed with an accepted method.
steps: Nucleus platform accepts the assertion and records the asserted method.

exception_flows.condition: The user fails the factor 5 times in a row.
exception_flows.handling: The factor is locked for 15 minutes, the session is ended and the tenant admin is alerted.

exception_flows.condition: A privileged user has no enrolled factor.
exception_flows.handling: Privileged functions are blocked and the user is taken to factor enrolment before continuing.

exception_flows.condition: The user cancels the step-up challenge.
exception_flows.handling: The protected action is abandoned and nothing is changed.

nfrs: Step-up challenge and verification complete in under 3 seconds at p95 excluding user think time.
Authentication flows conform to OWASP ASVS level 2 controls for authentication and session management.

user_stories.want: to confirm my identity again before approving a payroll
user_stories.so_that: an unattended session cannot be used to release salaries

acceptance.given: the payroll manager last completed MFA 40 minutes ago and the step-up window is 5 minutes
acceptance.when: they click Approve on the October 2026 run for payroll group HO

acceptance.then: no new challenge is shown and the audit entry records the earlier authentication time

user_stories.want: to require MFA for all privileged roles
user_stories.so_that: a leaked password alone cannot open payroll or role administration

acceptance.given: the payroll manager role is marked privileged and the user has no enrolled factor
acceptance.then: payroll screens are blocked and factor enrolment is presented first

acceptance.given: a user fails TOTP 5 times
acceptance.then: the factor is locked for 15 minutes and the tenant admin receives an alert

user_stories.so_that: my salary cannot be redirected by someone using my open session

acceptance.when: he submits a new bank account number
acceptance.then: a step-up challenge is required before the change is accepted for approval

acceptance.given: he cancels the challenge
acceptance.then: the bank account is unchanged and no approval request is created

use_cases.name: Deliver notifications through a channel matrix and preference centre
use_cases.goal: Deliver each workflow and system notification on the right channels, in the recipient's language and time preferences, with an auditable delivery log.

stakeholders.interest: Receives approval prompts promptly without a flood of low-value alerts.
Hears from the system in their language and not during rest hours.
Can prove that a mandatory notice was delivered.

use_cases.trigger: A domain event occurs that the notification matrix maps to one or more recipients.
preconditions: The notification matrix maps event types to recipient roles, channels and a mandatory flag.
Templates exist for each mapped event in each enabled language.
postconditions_success: Each recipient receives the notification on the resolved channels, and each attempt is in the delivery log with status.
postconditions_failure: Undeliverable notifications are retried on the fallback channel and remain visible in-app; failures are logged with reason.

main_flow.action: Configures the matrix: event type × recipient role × channels (in-app, email, push, SMS, business messaging) and a mandatory flag.
Sets personal preferences in the preference centre: language, quiet hours and daily digest for non-urgent items.
Receives a domain event, for example an approval step opened, and resolves recipients from the matrix.
Applies quiet hours and digest preferences unless the notification is flagged mandatory.
Renders the template in the recipient's language with the event's data.
Dispatches on each resolved channel and records each attempt with status in the delivery log.
Searches the delivery log by recipient, event or date to evidence delivery.

alternate_flows.condition: The notification falls in the recipient's quiet hours and is not mandatory.
steps: Nucleus platform holds the notification and adds it to the next digest or releases it when quiet hours end.

alternate_flows.condition: No template exists in the recipient's language.
steps: Nucleus platform renders the tenant default language and records the fallback in the delivery log.

exception_flows.condition: The primary channel reports a delivery failure.
exception_flows.handling: The notification is retried once, then sent on the configured fallback channel; the in-app copy always remains.

exception_flows.condition: An employee tries to opt out of a mandatory notification type.
exception_flows.handling: The opt-out is refused with an explanation that the notice is mandatory.

nfrs: Urgent notifications are dispatched within 30 seconds of the triggering event at p95.
Delivery log entries are retained for 3 years and searchable within 5 seconds.

user_stories.so_that: I am not disturbed after my shift and I can read every message

user_stories.so_that: I can evidence that a mandatory notice reached each worker

acceptance.then: 71 entries are listed with channel, delivery status and timestamp

use_cases.name: Design approval processes without code
use_cases.goal: Let tenant administrators author, simulate, publish and revert approval chains, conditions and SLAs on the shared approval engine without a code release.

stakeholders.interest: Process changes after a reorganisation take days, not a release cycle.
Amount-based thresholds route only material items to directors.
Every published version is effective-dated and reversible with history.

use_cases.trigger: The client needs a new approval process or a change to conditions, steps or SLAs.
preconditions: The tenant admin holds the process-designer permission.
The request type is registered with the shared approval engine and exposes its condition fields (for example amount and worker class).
postconditions_success: A new effective-dated chain version is live and the previous version is retained for reversal.
postconditions_failure: The draft is unpublished and the active version is unchanged.

main_flow.action: Opens the visual designer for a request type and starts a draft from the active chain version.
Adds or reorders steps and sets each step's approver resolution mode and SLA hours.
Adds conditions, for example a director step only when loan amount exceeds ₹2,00,000.
Validates that every path resolves an approver, has a reroute policy and ends in a terminal state.
Runs a simulation with sample requests and reviews the path and approvers each one would take.
Publishes the draft with an effective-from date and change reason.
Activates the version for new submissions from the effective date; in-flight instances stay on their starting version.

alternate_flows.condition: A published version needs to be reverted.
steps: Tenant admin selects the prior version and publishes it as a new version with a reversal reason.
Nucleus platform applies it to new submissions from the chosen date.

exception_flows.condition: A condition branch has no approver or no terminal state.
exception_flows.handling: Validation fails and highlights the incomplete branch on the canvas.

exception_flows.condition: A step is resolved by named person without a reroute policy.
exception_flows.handling: Validation fails until a successor or role fallback is set.

exception_flows.condition: The new version overlaps the keys of another active chain.
exception_flows.handling: Publication is blocked and the overlapping chain is named.

nfrs: The designer canvas remains responsive with up to 25 steps and 10 condition branches.
The designer meets WCAG 2.2 AA, including keyboard-only editing of steps.

acceptance.then: they continue on version 3 until closed

use_cases.name: Promote configuration from sandbox to production
use_cases.goal: Build and test configuration in a sandbox tenant and promote it to production as a reviewed, approved and reversible package.

stakeholders.interest: Nothing reaches production without a visible diff and approval.
Rule changes are tested on realistic data before a live run.
Each promotion is traceable to its package, approver and rollback point.

use_cases.trigger: A configuration change is ready for testing or for promotion to production.
preconditions: A sandbox tenant is linked to the production tenant.
Sandbox data containing personal information is masked or synthetic.
postconditions_success: Production holds the promoted configuration as new effective-dated versions, with a recorded rollback point.
postconditions_failure: Production configuration is unchanged, or restored to the rollback point.

main_flow.action: Refreshes the sandbox from production configuration with personal data masked.
Authors and tests changes to rules, picklists, workflows and rule packs in the sandbox.
Assembles the changed objects into a configuration package with a description.
Produces an object-by-object diff of the package against the production tenant and flags dependency gaps.
Reviews the diff and approves or rejects the promotion.
Records a rollback point and applies the package to production as new configuration versions.
Runs post-promotion smoke checks and records the result against the package.

alternate_flows.condition: Smoke checks pass but the client later asks to undo the promotion.
steps: Tenant admin selects the package and requests rollback with a reason.
Nucleus platform writes new versions restoring the rollback-point configuration.

exception_flows.condition: The package references an object missing in production, such as a picklist value.
exception_flows.handling: Promotion is blocked until the dependency is added to the package.

exception_flows.condition: A smoke check fails.
exception_flows.handling: The platform restores the rollback point automatically and marks the promotion Failed.

exception_flows.condition: Production changed the same object after the diff was produced.
exception_flows.handling: Promotion stops and a fresh diff is required.

nfrs: A package of 200 objects is diffed in under 30 seconds and applied in under 2 minutes.
Sandbox refresh never copies unmasked Aadhaar, PAN or bank values.

user_stories.want: to see an exact diff before promoting a package
user_stories.so_that: only intended changes reach production

acceptance.when: the diff is generated against production
acceptance.then: exactly two objects are listed with field-level before-and-after values

acceptance.given: the package references a new shift-group picklist value that does not exist in production
acceptance.then: it is blocked with the missing dependency named

user_stories.so_that: a bad configuration can be withdrawn without manual edits

acceptance.then: new versions restore the earlier configuration and the package shows status Rolled back

acceptance.given: a post-promotion smoke check fails
acceptance.then: the rollback point is restored automatically and the tenant admin is alerted

use_cases.name: Delegate approval authority and act as a user
use_cases.goal: Allow time-boxed, reason-coded delegation of approvals and audited act-as sessions, with the real actor always recorded.

stakeholders.interest: Requests are decided while the usual approver is away.
Support staff can diagnose issues as the user without sharing passwords.
Delegated and act-as actions name the real person who acted.

use_cases.trigger: An approver plans an absence, or a support engineer needs to reproduce a user's problem.
preconditions: The delegate holds a role that can view the delegated request types within the delegator's scope.
Act-as is enabled by the tenant admin for named support principals only.
postconditions_success: During the window, items route to the delegate, and every action records both delegate and delegator.
The delegation or act-as session ends automatically at its end time.
postconditions_failure: No delegation is created and items continue to route to the original approver.

main_flow.action: Creates a delegation naming the delegate, request types, start and end dates and a reason code.
Validates that the delegate is active, is not the requester on any delegated item, and has the scope to see the items.
From the start date, resolves steps owned by the delegator to the delegate and moves open items to the delegate's inbox.
As delegate, approves or rejects items; the decision records the delegate as actor and the delegator as on-behalf-of.
Ends the delegation at the end date and returns open items to the delegator's inbox.

alternate_flows.condition: A support engineer needs to act as a user to diagnose a problem.
steps: A support engineer requests an act-as session for a user with a ticket reference and a duration up to 60 minutes.
Tenant admin approves the session; Nucleus platform shows a persistent act-as banner and records every action with the real actor.
The session ends automatically at expiry.

alternate_flows.condition: The delegator returns early.
steps: Manager / supervisor ends the delegation before its end date.
Nucleus platform returns open items to the delegator immediately.

exception_flows.condition: The delegate has left or is inactive during the window.
exception_flows.handling: The delegation is suspended and items reroute to the successor or role holder.

exception_flows.condition: The delegated item was raised by the delegate.
exception_flows.handling: The item skips the delegate and resolves to the next approver in the line.

exception_flows.condition: An act-as session attempts to approve payroll or grant roles.
exception_flows.handling: The action is blocked in act-as sessions and the attempt is logged.

nfrs: Open items move to the delegate's inbox within 1 minute of the delegation start time.
Act-as sessions cannot exceed 60 minutes and cannot be extended without a new approval.

user_stories.want: to delegate my approvals to a colleague for my leave dates
user_stories.so_that: my team's requests are not delayed while I am away

use_cases.name: Load data in bulk with validation and rollback
use_cases.goal: Import master or transaction records in bulk, validated row by row with the same rules as the forms, with dry-run, partial-commit control and batch rollback.

stakeholders.interest: Large changes such as annual increments load in minutes, not days of manual entry.
Bad rows never reach payroll inputs.
Each load batch is identifiable and reversible.

use_cases.trigger: HR operations needs to create or update many records of one object type from a spreadsheet, CSV file or API call.
preconditions: The user holds create or update permission for the object within the target entity and location scope.
A load template exists for the object.
postconditions_success: Valid rows are committed under one batch ID, each as a versioned write, and a load report is stored.
postconditions_failure: No rows are committed in all-or-nothing mode; in partial mode only valid rows are committed and rejected rows are reported.

main_flow.action: Selects the object type, for example assignment changes, and downloads the load template.
Uploads the completed file or submits the API payload and chooses dry-run.
Validates every row with the same rules as the form, including scope checks, and builds a row-level report.
Reviews the dry-run report and corrects rejected rows or accepts them as excluded.
Chooses all-or-nothing or partial commit and confirms the load.
Commits rows as versioned writes tagged with the batch ID and stores the final load report.
Notifies HR operations with counts of committed, rejected and skipped rows.

alternate_flows.condition: HR operations discovers after commit that the batch was wrong.
steps: HR operations requests rollback of the batch with a reason.
Nucleus platform writes reversing versions for every row in the batch and marks the batch Rolled back.

exception_flows.condition: A row targets a record outside the user's entity or location scope.
exception_flows.handling: The row is rejected with a scope error; the user never learns whether the record exists.

exception_flows.condition: The file's column headers do not match the template.
exception_flows.handling: The whole file is rejected before row validation with the mismatched columns listed.

exception_flows.condition: All-or-nothing mode and any row fails at commit time.
exception_flows.handling: The whole batch is rolled back and the failing row is reported.

nfrs: A dry-run of 10,000 rows completes in under 2 minutes.
Rollback of a 10,000-row batch completes in under 5 minutes and leaves no partial state.

user_stories.want: a dry-run report before anything is saved
user_stories.so_that: I can fix errors without polluting live records

acceptance.when: HR operations requests rollback with reason 'Wrong increment file'
acceptance.then: all 497 records return to their prior values as new versions and the batch shows Rolled back

acceptance.given: the batch has been rolled back
acceptance.when: the version history of any affected record is opened
acceptance.then: both the loaded and the reversing versions are visible

user_stories.so_that: bulk import cannot be used to bypass access controls

use_cases.name: Add custom fields and custom objects
use_cases.goal: Let tenant administrators extend core objects with typed, validated, security-classified fields and objects without a schema release.

stakeholders.interest: Can capture client-specific data such as safety induction batch on the record.
A custom field classified as compensation is protected like other salary fields.
Custom field definitions are versioned and their changes audited.

use_cases.trigger: The client needs to capture data that the standard object model does not hold.
preconditions: The tenant admin holds the extension-administration permission.
The target core object supports extensions.
postconditions_success: The custom field or object is available on forms, in reports and through the API according to its security classification.
postconditions_failure: No definition is published and existing forms are unchanged.

main_flow.action: Selects the core object, for example assignment, and adds a field with name, type and validation.
Sets the security classification: general, personal, sensitive personal or compensation.
Chooses reporting and API exposure and the forms on which the field appears.
Validates name uniqueness, type and that compensation fields follow payroll-group visibility.
Publishes the definition with an effective-from date.
Renders the field on the chosen forms and applies the classification on every read path.

alternate_flows.condition: The data needs its own record type, such as a safety training register.
steps: Tenant admin defines a custom object with fields and a relationship to person or assignment.
Nucleus platform creates list and detail views for the object within entity and location scope.

exception_flows.condition: The field name collides with a standard or existing custom field.
exception_flows.handling: Publication is blocked with the conflicting name shown.

exception_flows.condition: A reader outside the record's payroll group requests a field classified as compensation.
exception_flows.handling: The field is returned as null, exactly as standard compensation fields are.

nfrs: Adding up to 50 custom fields to an object adds no more than 10% to form load time.
Custom fields are available in reports within 5 minutes of publication.

use_cases.name: Migrate data from a legacy HRMS and payroll system
use_cases.goal: Move master data, balances and year-to-date values from a legacy HRMS or payroll system with mapping, sequenced loads and reconciliation sign-off.

stakeholders.interest: Year-to-date earnings and deductions carry over exactly so the first live run is correct.
Leave balances and service history are preserved for every employee.
Migrated totals reconcile to the legacy system's closing figures.

use_cases.trigger: A client goes live and its history must be moved from the legacy system.
preconditions: The tenant is provisioned and core configuration (entities, locations, worker classes, pay components) is published.
Legacy extracts for the cut-over date are available.
postconditions_success: All in-scope records are loaded, reconciliation reports match within agreed tolerances, and the payroll manager has signed off.
postconditions_failure: Loaded batches are rolled back and the tenant returns to its pre-migration state.

main_flow.action: Selects the mapping template for the legacy source and maps each source field to a Nucleus field.
Defines transformation rules, such as legacy grade codes to designation and band.
Orders loads by dependency: org units, positions, persons, employments, assignments, salary, balances, then YTD values.
Runs each load as a dry-run batch with row-level validation and reports errors.
Corrects errors and commits each batch in sequence.
Produces reconciliation reports: record counts, leave balances and YTD earnings and deductions per employee and in total.
Reviews reconciliation against legacy closing figures and signs off or raises discrepancies.

alternate_flows.condition: Discrepancies exceed tolerance for some employees.
steps: Payroll manager lists the discrepant employees with expected values.
Implementation consultant corrects the mapping or source and reloads only the affected batch.

exception_flows.condition: A load references a parent that has not been loaded, such as an assignment for a missing position.
exception_flows.handling: The batch is held until its dependency loads successfully.

exception_flows.condition: Sign-off is refused at cut-over.
exception_flows.handling: All migration batches are rolled back in reverse order and go-live is postponed.

nfrs: A 10,000-employee migration with 3 years of history completes all loads within an 8-hour cut-over window.
Total YTD gross and statutory deductions reconcile to the legacy figures with zero variance.

user_stories.want: a reconciliation of YTD values against the legacy system before go-live
user_stories.so_that: the first live payroll's tax and statutory figures are right

use_cases.name: Handle a data-principal rights request
use_cases.goal: Receive, verify, track and fulfil access, correction, erasure and grievance requests from data principals, anonymising personal data while retaining statutory payroll records.

stakeholders.interest: Can see, correct or remove their personal data and complain if unhappy.
Requests are handled within the configured timeline and evidenced for the DPDP Act 2023 (to be validated by Legal).
Statutory payroll records needed for tax and audit survive erasure in anonymised form.

use_cases.trigger: A current or former employee, or a candidate, submits a data-principal request.
preconditions: The requester can be identified from an active account or through offline verification.
Retention periods per record class are configured by the Compliance owner.
postconditions_success: The request is fulfilled and closed with a response to the requester, and every step is in the audit ledger.
postconditions_failure: The request is closed as refused or partly fulfilled with the reason and the grievance route communicated.

main_flow.action: Submits a request choosing access, correction, erasure or grievance, with details.
Verifies identity with a step-up challenge, or routes to HR operations for offline verification for former employees.
Registers the request, starts the configured SLA clock and assigns it to the Compliance owner.
Triages the request and confirms the records and systems in scope.
For access, compiles the requester's personal data into a downloadable export.
Approves fulfilment and sends the response through the requester's channel.
Closes the request and records outcome and timeline in the audit ledger.

alternate_flows.condition: The request is a correction.
steps: Nucleus platform routes the correction through the approval chain for that field.
On approval, the correction is written as a new version with the request reference as reason.

alternate_flows.condition: The request is an erasure.
steps: Nucleus platform identifies records under a retention obligation, such as payroll registers and tax deductions.
It anonymises personal identifiers in all other records and replaces identity in retained payroll records with a pseudonymous key.
Compliance owner reviews the erasure report listing retained records and the reason for each.

exception_flows.condition: Identity verification fails.
exception_flows.handling: The request is held as Unverified and no data is disclosed or changed.

exception_flows.condition: The SLA is about to expire.
exception_flows.handling: The request escalates to the Compliance owner's manager at 80% of the SLA and the breach is counted if it expires.

nfrs: An access export for one person is generated within 10 minutes.
Erasure leaves no personal identifier in searchable indexes, caches or analytics stores, verified by an automated scan.

user_stories.want: to request a copy of my personal data from the self-service app
user_stories.so_that: I know what the employer holds about me

acceptance.then: E1043 receives a download of her personal data and the request closes with the date recorded

acceptance.then: it is held as Unverified and no data is compiled

acceptance.then: name, mobile, address and documents are anonymised and payroll register rows remain under a pseudonymous key

acceptance.then: each retained record class is listed with its retention reason

user_stories.so_that: no request is forgotten

acceptance.then: it escalates to the compliance owner's manager

use_cases.name: Provision identities to the enterprise directory
use_cases.goal: Create, update and disable user identities in downstream directories through SCIM 2.0 within 15 minutes of hire, transfer and exit events.

stakeholders.interest: Has working accounts on the first day.
Leavers lose access promptly and nobody keeps orphaned accounts.
Every provisioning call and result is logged.

use_cases.trigger: A hire, transfer or exit becomes effective in People Core.
preconditions: The tenant admin has configured a SCIM 2.0 connection to the enterprise directory and the attribute mapping.
The worker's assignment carries the attributes the directory needs, such as department and manager.
postconditions_success: The directory account matches the worker's current state, and the call result is logged within 15 minutes of the effective event.
postconditions_failure: The provisioning item is retried and, if still failing, raised to the tenant admin with the directory's error.

main_flow.action: Consumes a hire, assignment-change or exit event when it becomes effective.
Maps worker attributes to directory attributes: user name, display name, department, manager, location and active flag.
Sends the SCIM 2.0 create, update or deactivate request to the enterprise directory.
Applies the change and returns the result with the directory's identifier.
Stores the directory identifier and logs the call, payload digest and result.
Monitors the provisioning dashboard for pending, failed and completed items.

alternate_flows.condition: The event is an exit.
steps: Nucleus platform sends a deactivate request at the end of the last working day.
It also revokes Nucleus grants for the principal so access ends in both systems.

alternate_flows.condition: A hire is effective in the future.
steps: Nucleus platform schedules the create request for the start of the joining date, or earlier if pre-boarding access is configured.

exception_flows.condition: The directory returns a conflict because the user name exists.
exception_flows.handling: The item is held and raised to the tenant admin to confirm a link or a new user name.

exception_flows.condition: The directory is unreachable.
exception_flows.handling: The request is retried with backoff; if not completed within 15 minutes the item is flagged as an SLA breach.

nfrs: 95% of provisioning changes complete within 15 minutes of the effective event, measured monthly.
Deactivation on exit completes within 15 minutes of the end of the last working day.

user_stories.want: leavers' directory accounts to be disabled automatically
user_stories.so_that: no former employee keeps access to company systems
